Border.md.text:
# RDS Border Strategy

**Status:** Recommended decision — pending Rahino approval  
**Scope:** Rahino Design System and Qipper (Inventory, Finance, Project & Task Management)

## Decision

Adopt a **mostly borderless, semantic-boundary approach**, not a strict no-borders policy.

- **Spacing and typography** organize content.
- **Surface contrast** separates groups and static containers.
- **Borders** clarify controls, dense data, and interaction states.
- **Shadows** indicate actual elevation (menus, popovers, dialogs), not decorative cards.

This aligns with the restrained visual direction of products such as Linear, Notion, and Figma, without losing the clarity needed in dense tools such as Airtable and GitHub. These observations are drawn from publicly shown product interfaces, not exhaustive authenticated in-app audits.

## Component Rules

| Context                                   | RDS rule                                                                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --- |
| Page sections, standard cards, dashboards | Borderless by default; use spacing and surface contrast.                          |
| Text inputs, selects, other form controls | Clear boundary: recognizable filled treatment.                                    |
| Primary buttons                           | Filled; no border.                                                                |
| Secondary buttons                         | Subtle fill by default; outline only when necessary to communicate affordance.    |
| Toolbar / tertiary buttons                | Borderless but recognizably interactive.                                          |
| Inventory and finance tables              | **1px separators** as needed for readability; avoid boxing every cell.            |
| Task boards, selectable cards             | Surface-based cards; use an attention ring when selecting, dragging, or dropping. |
| Sidebars, headers, adjacent panels        | Surface change first; a single separator only when separation is unclear.         |     |
| Popovers, dropdowns, dialogs              | Raised surface plus existing RDS elevation token;                                 |
| Keyboard focus                            | **Independent 2px focus ring**, not a border-color change.                        |

**Constraints:** Avoid nested outlines and decorative card borders. A selected or invalid state must not be communicated through border color alone. Preserve functional controls and focus indicators on mobile even when outer card borders disappear.

## Final Minimal Token Set (Proposed)

These are **recommended token roles and starting values**, not claims about already approved RDS color tokens. Keep RDS's existing surface, focus-color, radius, and shadow foundations; do not introduce a second foundation for them.

| Token                      | Light                              | Dark                               | Meaning                                 |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --- |
| `rds.border.width.default` | `1px`                              | `1px`                              | Functional boundaries and separators    |
| `rds.border.width.strong`  | `2px`                              | `2px`                              | Emphasized selection / drop targets     |
| `rds.color.edge.subtle`    | `rgba(15,23,42,0.12)`              | `rgba(255,255,255,0.10)`           | Optional decorative dividers only       |
| `rds.color.edge.control`   | `#7A8493`                          | `#7A8493`                          | Recognizable form-control boundary      |
| `rds.focus.ring.width`     | `2px`                              | `2px`                              | Keyboard focus indicator                |     |
| `rds.color.focus.ring`     | **Alias existing RDS focus color** | **Alias existing RDS focus color** | Do not add unrelated blue accent colors |

boundaries required to identify a control or state must meet **WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast ≥ 3:1**. Focus indicators must remain clearly visible.

**No extra tokens:** Do not keep a large legacy `edge.*` family unless a documented component need justifies a distinct role. Do not copy research-proposed radius, surface, or shadow scales into RDS.

## Validation Before Approval

Test one representative **Inventory grid**, **Finance form**, **Task board**, and **Settings page**, each in light/dark mode, keyboard navigation, mobile, and RTL. Check scanning, control discoverability, focus, selected/error states, and excessive nested containers.

## References

- [Material 3 — Card variants](https://m3.material.io/components/cards/overview)
- [Microsoft Fluent 2 — Elevation](https://fluent2.microsoft.design/elevation)
- [NN/g — Recognizable clickable elements](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/clickable-elements/)
- [W3C — Non-text contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)
- [W3C — Focus visible](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-visible.html)

Layout.md.text:
# Rahino Design System — Layout & Responsiveness

**Status:** Final foundation decisions.

Change the layout structure as space changes. Keep the current task clear and preserve necessary information and actions.

## 1. Units

| Property | Unit |
| --- | --- |
| Breakpoints, typography sizes and reading measure | `rem` |
| Spacing, gutters, margins and fixed dimensions | `px` |
| Line-height | Unitless |
| Flexible dimensions | `%`, `fr`, `auto`, `minmax()` |

Keep the root font size at `100%`. Use existing spacing and typography tokens.

## 2. Page grid

| Range | Width | Columns | Gutter | Minimum page margin per side |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Narrow | Below `48rem` | 4 | 16px | 16px |
| Medium | `48rem` to below `64rem` | 8 | 24px | 24px |
| Wide | `64rem` and above | 12 | 24px | 32px |

At a 16px browser default, the breakpoints equal **768px** and **1024px**.

**Page margin** is the space between content and the edges of its available area. **Gutter** is the space between columns. Margins may grow when content reaches its maximum width.

Columns guide alignment; they do not determine the number of cards or fields.

Page margins apply to main content. The **sidebar, header and footer have 0px outer margin**. Their internal padding is defined separately.

## 3. Content width

| Content | Maximum width |
| --- | ---: |
| Reading | 42rem |
| Marketing page | 1600px |
| Dashboard | 1600px |
| Tables and editors needing more space | Available width |
| Forms | Defined by the form recipe; no universal cap |

Content fills available space up to its cap. Caps exclude page margins and app navigation. Reading text keeps its own cap inside wider layouts.

**Reading measure:** Use `rds.type.layout.measure.reading` as the single maximum for long-form text: `42rem`, equivalent to 672px when the root font size is 16px. Reading content fills its available width up to this cap and can shrink below it; never force a 42rem-wide column on a narrow container. The rem cap follows changes to the browser's default font size. A wider page, dashboard or marketing container does not increase the reading-text cap. There is no separate 48rem reading preset.

## 4. Essential rules

| Area | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Hierarchy | Primary task → supporting information → readable secondary metadata. One dominant action per task region. |
| Grouping | Use spacing, headings and surface contrast first; add shadows or borders only when needed. |
| Nested layouts | Fit the container. Use only the columns and internal padding needed. |
| Responsive structure | Stack columns and supporting panels when space is insufficient. Keep actions and navigation accessible. |
| Queries | Viewport queries for the app shell; container queries for reusable components. No universal component thresholds. |
| Spacing and density | Switch between existing spacing tokens. Regular is default; Spacious is optional. Width does not select density. |
| Typography | Keep approved typography sizes; only designated headings are viewport-fluid. Allow text and controls to grow. |
| Direction | Support RTL and LTR with reading order and alignment appropriate to the content. |
| Reflow | Remain usable at 320px, 200% text resizing and 400% browser zoom. Wide tables may scroll locally. |

Exact navigation behavior, form layouts and component breakpoints belong in their recipes.

**References:** [Spectrum spacing](https://spectrum.adobe.com/foundations/layout-and-structure/spacing/layout-spacing) · [Spectrum containers](https://spectrum.adobe.com/foundations/layout-and-structure/containers) · [USWDS typography](https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/typography/) · [WCAG reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/reflow.html)

These references inform the principles; the numeric defaults above are RDS decisions.


**Reading-width rationale:** The 42rem value preserves Rahino's existing 672px baseline at a 16px root while following the typography unit policy. Relative reading measures are used by [USWDS](https://designsystem.digital.gov/design-tokens/typesetting/measure/); [WCAG visual-presentation guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/visual-presentation.html) emphasizes manageable line lengths and resizable columns. Neither source mandates 42rem. Check actual Persian, English and mixed-script line lengths using the approved fonts; this cap alone does not guarantee a particular character count.

## 5. Shared layout tokens

The approved values above are exported from [layout.ts](layout.ts). That file is generated from the master token collection; update the master and regenerate rather than editing exported values separately.

| Public token family | TypeScript export | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rds.layout.breakpoint.*` | `BREAKPOINTS` | Medium and wide inclusive lower bounds |
| `rds.layout.grid.*` | `PAGE_GRID` | Columns, gutters and minimum page margins for each range |
| `rds.layout.content.max` | `PAGE_MAX_WIDTH` | Shared marketing-page and dashboard cap |

All 12 token definitions and their values appear in the generated [master list](master-tokens/Master-Token-List.md).

The medium and wide breakpoint values are inclusive lower bounds: narrow is below 48rem, medium is 48rem to below 64rem, and wide starts at 64rem. These names identify the existing page-grid ranges, not device categories. In media queries, use the generated literal breakpoint values; CSS custom properties cannot be substituted into media-query conditions.

Gutter and margin values alias existing shared spacing. Reading width continues to use `rds.type.layout.measure.reading` through `TEXT_LAYOUT.measure.reading` in Typography.ts; no duplicate layout reading token is introduced. Available-width behavior, form recipes, zero outer margins on app chrome, and responsive composition remain documented rules.

Motion.md.text:
# Rahino Design System — Motion & Interaction

**Status:** Phase one — visual motion testing in Figma completed (confirmed by the foundation owner). Qipper implementation testing remains pending.

## 1. Design Principle

Motion in Rahino must feel **natural, responsive, precise, and unobtrusive**.

Animation should provide feedback, clarify state changes, or preserve continuity not attract attention.

**Interaction always takes priority over animation.**

## 2. Motion Tokens

| Token        | Duration | Usage                                          |
| ------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Dissolve     | 150ms    | Immediate state update, Navigation transitions |
| Feedback     | 150ms    | Hover, pressed, color changes, Toggles         |
| Overlay      | 240ms    | Popovers, menus, Dialogs                       |
| Reduced      | 0–80ms   | Reduced-motion feedback                        |
| Presentation | 480ms    | Nonessential expressive motion                 |

Exits should generally take **75–85% of entry duration**. Adjust durations only when interaction scale or spatial distance justifies it.

## 3. Easing

| Token    | Value                            |
| -------- | -------------------------------- |
| Standard | `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1)`    |
| Enter    | `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)` |
| Exit     | `cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.56, 1)`  |
| Linear   | `linear`                         |

Avoid bounce, elastic, overshoot, and exaggerated spring effects in functional interfaces.

## 4. Interaction Rules

- **Immediate feedback:** Never delay interaction for animation.
- **Buttons:** Use subtle color or elevation transitions. Press scaling is optional, with a minimum scale of 0.98.
- **Popovers and menus:** Use opacity with a maximum 2–4px translation.
- **Dialogs:** Use opacity with up to 8px translation or scale from 0.98. Avoid combining effects unnecessarily.
- **Navigation:** Animate only when it improves orientation. Keep persistent UI stable.
- **Tables and forms:** Prioritize stability. Avoid animated numbers, staggered rows, and unnecessary layout movement.
- **Loading:** Never introduce artificial delays. Use meaningful progress indicators or stable placeholders when necessary.

## 5. Motion Behavior

- Motion must reinforce spatial relationships and interaction direction, including RTL.
- Animations must be interruptible and reversible from their current state.
- Repeated interactions must not queue animations or cause visual jumps.
- Avoid unnecessary entrance animations, cascading reveals, parallax, and decorative movement.
- Do not animate elements simply because they appear on screen.

## 6. Accessibility & Performance

- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: remove nonessential movement and scaling; allow up to 80ms opacity feedback when useful.
- Never communicate essential information through motion alone.
- Prefer `transform` and `opacity` for movement.
- Avoid `transition: all`, expensive layout animations, and frequent blur effects.
- Target smooth 60fps interactions on representative devices without compromising input responsiveness.
- Use shared motion tokens consistently across components.

## 7. Brand Consistency

Rahino's motion language should feel **calm, confident, fluid, and purposeful**.

Expressive animations belong primarily in landing pages and presentation experiences, not everyday product workflows.

## 8. Validation

**Phase one — completed:** Visual motion testing in Figma. This status is based on the foundation owner's confirmation; it does not establish browser behavior, device performance or production accessibility.

**Implementation testing — pending:** Verify the motion in Qipper components, particularly buttons, menus, dialogs, navigation and data tables. Include rapid repeated interactions, interrupted transitions, RTL, keyboard navigation, reduced motion and lower-powered devices before release.

**Core rule: If motion doesn't improve usability, don't animate.**

Motion.ts.text:
/**
 * Rahino Design System — Motion & interaction foundations
 *
 * Source: Motion.md.
 * Status: Phase one visual motion testing in Figma completed, as confirmed
 * by the foundation owner. Qipper implementation testing remains pending.
 * Figma validation does not establish production behavior or release approval.
 *
 * Naming follows the reference foundations pattern:
 *   rds.motion.duration.feedback -> --rds-motion-duration-feedback
 *   rds.motion.easing.enter      -> --rds-motion-easing-enter
 *   rds.motion.scale.subtle      -> --rds-motion-scale-subtle
 *
 * Scope: descriptive TypeScript contract, with CSS-ready durations/distances
 * and unitless scale values. Motion values are shared across light/dark modes.
 * JSDoc is not a DTCG-conformant typed registry; generate future platform
 * outputs from the canonical registry rather than maintaining duplicate tables.
 */

/** @family rds.motion.duration */
export const DURATION = {
  /**
   * @token rds.motion.duration.none
   * @usage No animated transition; the lower endpoint of the documented
   *        reduced-motion range (0–80ms).
   * @a11y Remove nonessential motion instead of merely shortening it.
   */
  none: "0ms",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.duration.dissolve
   * @usage Immediate state updates and navigation transitions when motion
   *        improves orientation. Keep persistent navigation UI stable.
   * @avoid Animating every route change or delaying an immediate update.
   */
  dissolve: "150ms",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.duration.feedback
   * @usage Hover, pressed, color changes, toggles, and subtle elevation
   *        transitions. Separate from dissolve despite the equal value.
   * @avoid Artificial interaction delays or mandatory press scaling.
   */
  feedback: "150ms",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.duration.overlay
   * @usage Entry timing for popovers, menus, and dialogs.
   * @rules Exit timing generally uses 75–85% of entry duration.
   * @avoid Applying the same full duration indiscriminately to every exit.
   */
  overlay: "240ms",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.duration.reduced
   * @usage Upper bound for useful opacity feedback under reduced motion.
   *        Choose no transition or a duration within 0–80ms as appropriate.
   * @a11y Remove nonessential movement and scaling entirely. This token
   *       does not authorize translating/scaling an element for 80ms.
   */
  reduced: "80ms",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.duration.presentation
   * @usage Optional nonessential expressive motion, primarily in landing
   *        pages and presentation experiences.
   * @avoid Everyday product workflows and decorative product entrances.
   * @a11y Remove this motion when prefers-reduced-motion is active.
   */
  presentation: "480ms",
} as const;

/** @family rds.motion.easing */
export const EASING = {
  /**
   * @token rds.motion.easing.standard
   * @usage Standard easing for state transitions and interaction feedback.
   * @avoid Bounce, elastic, overshoot, or exaggerated spring replacements.
   */
  standard: "cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.58, 1)",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.easing.enter
   * @usage Elements entering a view or overlay becoming visible.
   * @avoid Adding an entrance animation solely because content appears.
   */
  enter: "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.easing.exit
   * @usage Elements leaving a view or overlay being dismissed.
   * @rules Select exit timing separately from the easing curve.
   */
  exit: "cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.56, 1)",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.easing.linear
   * @usage Constant-rate animation when constant progression is intended.
   * @avoid Treating linear as the default for every interaction.
   */
  linear: "linear",
} as const;

/**
 * @family rds.motion.translation
 * Unsigned magnitudes from the documented interaction limits, not mandatory
 * travel distances. Choose the axis/sign from the actual spatial relationship,
 * including RTL. Opacity-only transitions can use no translation at all.
 */
export const TRANSLATION = {
  /**
   * @token rds.motion.translation.popover-subtle
   * @usage Optional 2px translation with opacity for popovers and menus.
   * @rules Lower endpoint of the documented 2–4px translation guidance;
   *        not a required minimum movement.
   * @a11y Remove translation under reduced motion.
   */
  "popover-subtle": "2px",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.translation.popover-max
   * @usage Maximum optional translation for popovers and menus.
   * @avoid Movement greater than 4px or unnecessary combined effects.
   * @a11y Remove translation under reduced motion.
   */
  "popover-max": "4px",

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.translation.dialog-max
   * @usage Maximum optional dialog translation, paired with opacity.
   * @rules Use translation or subtle scale when helpful; avoid combining
   *        effects unnecessarily.
   * @avoid Treating 8px movement as mandatory for every dialog.
   * @a11y Remove translation under reduced motion.
   */
  "dialog-max": "8px",
} as const;

/**
 * @family rds.motion.scale
 * Unitless transform factors. Scaling is an optional, explicit component
 * behavior, not a global button rule or a default entrance treatment.
 */
export const SCALE = {
  /**
   * @token rds.motion.scale.subtle
   * @usage Opt-in press feedback for selected controls, or a dialog's
   *        starting scale when subtle scaling improves the interaction.
   * @rules 0.98 is the documented minimum scale; do not shrink further.
   *        Buttons normally use subtle color/elevation feedback. Dialogs
   *        may pair opacity with scale from 0.98 to 1 instead of translation.
   * @avoid Applying scale to all buttons, table rows, forms, or persistent UI.
   * @a11y Remove scaling under reduced motion; use rest scale directly.
   */
  subtle: 0.98,

  /**
   * @token rds.motion.scale.rest
   * @usage Unscaled rest state and endpoint of optional subtle scaling.
   * @rules Identity transform, not an additional expressive scale preset.
   */
  rest: 1,
} as const;

export type DurationName = keyof typeof DURATION;
export type EasingName = keyof typeof EASING;
export type TranslationName = keyof typeof TRANSLATION;
export type ScaleName = keyof typeof SCALE;

Numbers.md.text:
# Numbers

## Display & formatting

- Use **Persian digits** (`۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹`) and symbols: thousands `٬`, decimal `٫`, percent `٪`, minus `−`—regardless of currency. Identifiers such as `INV-1042` remain unchanged.
- Isolate the numeric value with `<bdi dir="ltr">`; keep its unit separate. **Right-align financial values** without changing the direction of the whole table.
- Display dates in the **Solar Hijri calendar** when using the Persian date format. Timezone handling must preserve the intended calendar day.

| Type | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Negative amount | −۱۲٬۵۰۰ تومان |
| Foreign currency | ۱۲٬۵۰۰ دلار |
| Percentage | ۱۸٪ |
| Date | ۱۴۰۵/۰۷/۱۵ |

## Precision & data integrity

- Define decimal precision by profile: `money`, `quantity`, `rate`, `percent`, `metric`, `technical`. **Do not apply two decimal places globally.**
- The `percent` profile must explicitly specify whether its input is a **0–1 ratio** or an **already-scaled percentage**.
- **Qipper defaults to toman; Keeper Ledger defaults to rial.** Changing display units is not currency conversion; FX conversion is outside the formatter.
- Store monetary values precisely. Display rounding must never change the stored value, and ambiguous input must not be guessed.
- Distinguish **zero**, **missing data**, and **privacy-hidden values**. Show full amounts in financial reports (no compact notation).

## Typography

Reuse the existing [Typography](https://design.rahino.co/foundations/typography) roles; do not create a separate numerical type scale.

| Context | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Table values | `rds.type.ui-sm` |
| Totals | `rds.type.title-sm` |
| Standard KPI | `rds.type.title-md` |
| Compact / narrow KPI | `rds.type.title-sm` |
| Secondary numeric metadata | `rds.type.caption-md` |

IRANYekanX has no Persian tabular figures (`tnum`). Do not assume equal-width digits; test alignment with real values. Do not use `display` for routine dashboard KPIs.

Radius.md.text:
# Radius & Rounding

Rahino uses restrained rounding for controls and softer corners for larger surfaces. Radius is independent of typography, color, borders, and elevation.

## Radius tokens

All primitive values use `px`. Token names reflect their actual values and remain the same across themes, viewports, and density modes.

| Token             |          Value | Usage                                |
| ----------------- | -------------: | ------------------------------------ |
| `rds.radius.0`    |            0px | Sharp and attached edges             |
| `rds.radius.4`    |            4px | Checkboxes, tiny controls            |
| `rds.radius.8`    |            8px | Buttons, inputs, regular controls    |
| `rds.radius.12`   |           12px | Groups, small cards                  |
| `rds.radius.16`   |           16px | Panels, popovers, larger cards       |
| `rds.radius.24`   |           24px | Dialogs, sheets                      |
| **Full (recipe)** | **Height ÷ 2** | Chips, pills, fully rounded controls |

**Full** is a shape rule, not a fixed numeric primitive token. Use `border-radius: 9999px` for pills in CSS (the browser limits the effective radius to the shape); use half the component height in Figma. For a circle, use `50%` on an element with equal width and height.

## Rounding rules

- **Default:** Use 8px for regular controls. Do not make every button or input a pill.
- **Nested corners:** Inner radius should generally be smaller than outer radius. Account for inset spacing and prioritize visual balance over rigid formulas.
- **Attached edges:** Use 0px where a surface joins the viewport or an adjacent surface. A bottom sheet may have only its top corners rounded.
- **Responsive:** Keep radius values stable across breakpoints. Change a component's radius only if its geometry or layout pattern changes.
- **Density:** Regular and Spacious modes share the same radius tokens; increased spacing alone does not justify more rounding.
- **Exceptions:** Sharp corners are appropriate for some data visualizations, precision elements, and connected layouts.

## Implementation

Consume numeric radius tokens through their CSS variables (for example, `--rds-radius-8`). Apply **Full** only in component recipes that call for chips, pills, or circles; do not create a separate numeric radius for every component, theme, viewport, or density mode.

Radius.ts.text:
/**
 * Rahino Design System — Radius foundations (review-ready source)
 *
 * Canonical numeric naming matches the actual pixel value:
 *   rds.radius.0  -> --rds-radius-0
 *   rds.radius.8  -> --rds-radius-8
 *   rds.radius.24 -> --rds-radius-24
 *
 * Scope: fixed-radius primitives for component recipes. Radius is independent
 * of appearance (light/dark), responsive breakpoints, and density modes.
 * Geometry-dependent full rounding is a recipe, not a numeric primitive.
 *
 * USAGE NOTE: JSDoc describes the contract but is NOT a DTCG-conformant token
 * registry. If RDS adopts a machine-readable SSOT, publish $type/$value and
 * generate CSS, documentation, and design-tool outputs from that source.
 * Avoid maintaining independent handwritten values across outputs.
 *
 * Focus ring width/offset and border widths belong to their own foundations,
 * not to rds.radius; these values are documented in rahino-radius.md.
 */

/**
 * @family rds.radius
 * Fixed, theme-independent corner radii. Use primitive values in component
 * recipes; do not infer radius from elevation, density, or viewport width.
 */
export const RADIUS = {
  /**
   * @token rds.radius.0
   * @usage Sharp corners, viewport-attached edges, adjoining surfaces,
   *        and precision-oriented elements where rounding is inappropriate.
   * @avoid Using sharp corners randomly among otherwise matching components.
   */
  "0": "0px",

  /**
   * @token rds.radius.4
   * @usage Checkboxes and very small controls needing restrained rounding.
   * @avoid Default buttons, cards, and large containers.
   */
  "4": "4px",

  /**
   * @token rds.radius.8
   * @usage Default buttons, inputs, and regular interactive controls.
   * @avoid Replacing the full-rounding recipe for chips and pills.
   */
  "8": "8px",

  /**
   * @token rds.radius.12
   * @usage Grouped controls, compact cards, and smaller nested surfaces.
   * @avoid Automatically applying to every small component.
   */
  "12": "12px",

  /**
   * @token rds.radius.16
   * @usage Panels, popovers, and larger cards; pair floating surfaces with
   *        their appropriate surface and elevation roles.
   * @avoid Using radius alone to communicate elevation or separation.
   */
  "16": "16px",

  /**
   * @token rds.radius.24
   * @usage Dialogs and sheets where geometry permits rounded outer corners.
   * @avoid Rounding sheet edges that attach flush to the viewport.
   */
  "24": "24px",
} as const;

/**
 * @recipe full rounding — no rds.radius.full primitive
 * @usage Chips, pills, and fully rounded control variants. In Figma, use
 *        a radius equal to half the component height. For circles, ensure
 *        equal width and height and use 50% instead.
 * @avoid Using 50% for rectangular pills or treating 9999px as a literal
 *        visual radius; CSS normalizes the effective rounding to the box.
 *
 * CSS implementation shortcut, separate from the numeric token family.
 */
export const FULL_RADIUS_CSS = "9999px" as const;

Rahino-Tokenization.md.text:
# Rahino Design System — Tokenization Rules

**Principle:** A token records a reusable design decision, not every possible value. Keep one source of truth and add tokens only when they have a clear purpose.

## Token layers

| Layer | Prefix | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reference | `ref` | Raw values and scales, without usage meaning |
| Shared | `rds` | Stable semantic roles and approved shared scales |
| Component-specific | `recipe` | Decisions genuinely unique to one component |

**Spacing contract:** `ref.space.*` is the raw reference layer; `rds.space.*` is the shared semantic layer. Shared tokens alias the reference values using Spectrum's global spacing indexes. No spacing prefix exception is used.

Components use shared tokens first. Following Spectrum's component-specific approach, introduce `recipe` tokens only where shared tokens cannot express a real component requirement. A component recipe (composition and behavior) is **not** itself a token; do not tokenize every CSS property.

## Naming and values

- Use lowercase English paths separated by dots; use kebab-case within a path segment. Names describe **roles**, not temporary values, products, or viewports.
- Keep reference names tied to their actual value where that convention is defined. Shared tokens may provide a named scale rather than a new semantic role for each use.
- **Spacing example:** `ref.space.16` stores `16px`; `rds.space.300` aliases `{ref.space.16}`. Likewise, `rds.space.25` aliases `{ref.space.1}`. Use the full Spectrum index mapping in [Spacing](Spacing.md); `rds.space.0` → `{ref.space.0}` preserves Rahino's existing zero reset. Do not create separate semantic tokens for every gap.
- Use `px` for physical dimensions (spacing, radius, borders, focus, blur and shadow geometry); `rem` for typography dimensions and breakpoints; `ms` for time; unitless numbers for ratios, alpha and scale.
- **Reading-paragraph recipe exception:** `rds.type.layout.gap.paragraph` retains the existing `1em` CSS behavior only between consecutive reading paragraphs. Record the proportional rule as a CSS recipe outside ordinary DTCG dimension tokens; `em` is not a supported DTCG dimension unit. Preserve its public export without converting it to a fixed 16px gap. General interface spacing continues to use the px-based shared spacing scale. See [Typography](Typography.md#reading-paragraph-spacing).
- A token's meaning remains distinct even when its value equals another token's value.

## Canonical format and publishing

- Maintain **one canonical typed token source** using DTCG `$type`, `$value`, `$description`, and project metadata under `$extensions.rahino` when needed.
- Represent dotted public paths as nested groups in DTCG files. Use typed aliases instead of repeating shared values.
- Keep theme/context selection in manifests and the [Resolver rules](Rahino-Resolver.md), not in token names or a custom `$modes` field.
- Generate CSS variables, TypeScript exports, Figma mappings and documentation *value tables* from the canonical source. Do not maintain parallel hand-edited values.
- Keep public mapping consistent (for example, `rds.color.ink.primary` → `--rds-color-ink-primary` → `rds/color/ink/primary`).

## Adding and changing tokens

1. **Reuse** an existing token first; then consider a component-specific token; add a new shared role only for a distinct, recurring need.
2. Record the token's purpose, owner, actual consumers and any usage constraints. Experimental raw values are allowed only with an explicit review plan.
3. Before changing a public token, check affected components, aliases, modes, documentation and exported APIs. A value change must preserve its role; otherwise introduce a new role.
4. For a rename, merge or removal, document the **old → new** mapping and update consumers. Keep temporary compatibility aliases only when needed, with an explicit removal plan. Flag breaking changes for release review.
5. Remove unused or obsolete tokens only after checking real references and confirming that a migration is safe.

## Validation and maintenance

- Reject duplicate public names, missing or cyclic aliases, incompatible types, invalid units, and unsupported context combinations during build.
- Keep token definitions, generated outputs and usage documentation synchronized; test affected consumers after changes.
- Review token ownership and usage periodically. Prefer retiring redundancy over expanding the core without evidence.
- Do not publish breaking token changes or alter established design decisions without review and approval.

**References:** [Spectrum design tokens](https://spectrum.adobe.com/foundations/design-data/design-tokens) · [DTCG format](https://www.designtokens.org/tr/2025.10/format/)

Shadow.ts.text:
/**
 * Rahino Design System — Shadow foundations (review-ready source)
 *
 * Canonical token paths:
 *   rds.shadow.sm  -> --rds-shadow-sm
 *   rds.shadow.md  -> --rds-shadow-md
 *   rds.shadow.lg  -> --rds-shadow-lg
 *
 * Default surfaces do not receive a shadow. Choose elevation by behavior,
 * not component dimensions: a large static card can remain flat while a
 * small dropdown needs a contextual shadow.
 *
 * Shadow expresses visual elevation; z-index controls stacking order.
 * Coordinate them without treating them as interchangeable. Apply one
 * shadow token per surface rather than stacking multiple elevation tokens.
 *
 * JSDoc describes usage, but is not itself a DTCG token registry. Export
 * typed shadow values from one canonical source for CSS and Figma.
 */

export type AppearanceName = "light" | "dark";

/** Light/Dark projection consumed by existing foundations CSS generation. */
export interface Pair {
  light: string;
  dark: string;
}

const pair = (light: string, dark: string): Pair => ({ light, dark });

/**
 * @family rds.shadow
 * Behavioral elevation scale. Use no shadow for ordinary page sections,
 * table rows, form controls, and standard layout containers. Rely on surface
 * contrast, spacing, and optional functional boundaries first.
 *
 * Use lg for modal and confirmation dialogs and other prominent floating
 * panels. The three-level scale ends at lg.
 */
export const SHADOW = {
  /**
   * @token rds.shadow.sm
   * @role Subtle elevation
   * @usage Raised cards when elevation is needed, interactive card hover,
   *        sticky headers/toolbars above scrolling content, and buttons
   *        whose elevation is explicitly part of their component recipe.
   * @avoid Default shadows on every card, table row, or form control.
   */
  sm: pair(
    "0 2px 6px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.06)",
    "0 2px 6px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.14)",
  ),

  /**
   * @token rds.shadow.md
   * @role Contextual floating surfaces
   * @usage Dropdown menus, select menus, popovers, date pickers,
   *        autocomplete panels, floating tooltips, and toasts.
   * @avoid Ordinary in-flow cards or permanently elevated page sections.
   */
  md: pair(
    "0 8px 20px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.10)",
    "0 8px 20px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.20)",
  ),

  /**
   * @token rds.shadow.lg
   * @role Modal elevation
   * @usage Large navigation flyouts, modal and confirmation dialogs,
   *        expanded contextual panels, and non-modal floating drawers.
   * @avoid Static layout sections or elevating ordinary containers by default.
   *        This is the maximum shadow level for modal and non-modal surfaces.
   */
  lg: pair(
    "0 16px 36px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.14)",
    "0 16px 36px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.26)",
  ),
} as const;

Spacing.md.text:
# Rahino Design System — Spacing

**Status:** Agreed foundation decisions  
**Reference:** [Adobe Spectrum — Layout spacing](https://spectrum.adobe.com/foundations/layout-and-structure/spacing/layout-spacing)

## 1. Reference and shared spacing scale

- **Reference tokens:** `ref.space.<px>` stores the fixed raw value, using its actual size in the name: `ref.space.16` = `16px`.
- **Shared semantic tokens:** `rds.space.<index>` aliases a reference token. Positive indexes match Spectrum's published global spacing numbers; indexes are labels, not pixel values.
- Use the same shared scale for internal component spacing and page layouts. Typical uses are guidance, not predefined component recipes.

| Reference token | Shared semantic token | Value | Typical use |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `ref.space.0` | `rds.space.0` | 0px | Remove spacing |
| `ref.space.1` | `rds.space.25` | 1px | Exceptional optical adjustments |
| `ref.space.2` | `rds.space.50` | 2px | Very small internal adjustments |
| `ref.space.4` | `rds.space.75` | 4px | Tight label relationships |
| `ref.space.6` | `rds.space.85` | 6px | Fine component spacing |
| `ref.space.8` | `rds.space.100` | 8px | Icon-label gaps, related elements |
| `ref.space.12` | `rds.space.200` | 12px | Small component and group gaps |
| `ref.space.16` | `rds.space.300` | 16px | Fields, small containers |
| `ref.space.20` | `rds.space.350` | 20px | Intermediate padding |
| `ref.space.24` | `rds.space.400` | 24px | Standard containers, content groups |
| `ref.space.32` | `rds.space.500` | 32px | Spacious containers, major groups |
| `ref.space.40` | `rds.space.600` | 40px | Larger layout separation |
| `ref.space.48` | `rds.space.700` | 48px | Page sections |
| `ref.space.56` | `rds.space.750` | 56px | Larger section separation |
| `ref.space.64` | `rds.space.800` | 64px | Major layout regions |
| `ref.space.80` | `rds.space.900` | 80px | Large-scale composition |
| `ref.space.96` | `rds.space.1000` | 96px | Exceptional large layouts |

All 16 positive mappings match Spectrum. The `0 → 0px` pair preserves Rahino's existing reset and is a Rahino extension; Spectrum's table begins at `25 → 1px`.

Use **1–2px only for exceptional fine adjustments**, not normal layout gaps. Add new reference values only when a real use case justifies them.

In DTCG, `rds.space.300` aliases `{ref.space.16}`. In CSS, `--rds-space-300` references `var(--ref-space-16)`. In TypeScript, `SPACE[16]` remains the raw reference value and `SPACING[300]` references it. Components use shared `rds.space.*` tokens.

## 2. Density

- **Regular** is the default. **Spacious** is optional where useful. **Compact is removed as a named density**.
- **One-step adjustment rule:** To make a component more compact, decrease each spacing token used in its recipe by **one step** on the listed scale (not by arithmetic on token indexes); to make it more spacious, increase each by **one step** (e.g. `12px → 16px`). Apply this when defining and reviewing component recipes, not as an automatic global change. Preserve touch targets and other usability requirements.
- Density applies deliberately to eligible components, collections, or containers; it does **not** automatically affect nested controls.
- Not every component needs both densities. Spacious does not automatically change component sizes, font sizes, or line-heights.

## 3. Usage and responsive behavior

- **Internal spacing:** Component specifications choose padding and gap values from the shared scale, which aliases the reference values.
- **Layout spacing:** Smaller gaps group related content; larger gaps separate independent regions.
- **Reading-paragraph exception:** Consecutive paragraphs in reading content use the text-relative `1em` recipe documented in [Typography](Typography.md#reading-paragraph-spacing). This does not change the fixed spacing scale or interface-element gaps.
- **Responsive:** Primitive values stay fixed. A component or layout may switch between approved values based on available space; prefer container context when practical. Do not create separate mobile/desktop scales.
- **Fluid spacing:** No global `rds.space.fluid` token. A documented layout recipe may use `clamp()` for exceptional page-level needs (e.g. gutters), with approved scale values as endpoints. Ordinary component spacing stays token-based.
- **Accessibility:** Let content grow and reflow under text zoom; maintain usable touch targets and appropriate safe-area spacing.
- **Rahino visual direction:** In mostly borderless interfaces, use spacing, typography, and subtle surface contrast for hierarchy without making data-heavy screens unnecessarily spacious.

## 4. Token architecture

- **Spacing foundation (`Spacing.ts`):** Defines **17 reference tokens** in `SPACE` and **17 shared aliases** in `SPACING`. All physical values are unchanged.
- **Shared layer:** `rds.space.*` uses the Spectrum indexes above and explicitly aliases `ref.space.*`. Keep reference names tied to physical sizes and shared indexes tied to the approved scale.
- **Component specifications:** Reuse the shared spacing layer first. Define component-specific aliases, density recipes, and component sizing rules **as each component is created and validated**, not in advance.

## 5. Naming migration

The previous raw `rds.space.<px>` names move to `ref.space.<px>`. Shared tokens now use `rds.space.<Spectrum index>`; the earlier `rds.spacing.300` alias is superseded by `rds.space.300`. See the complete [old → new mapping](master-tokens/Spacing-Migration.md). These public token/CSS renames require consumer migration before release. The existing TypeScript `SPACE` and `SPACING` export names are retained.

Typography.md.text:
# Typography

Rahino uses one semantic typography scale across desktop, tablet, and mobile. Choose a **role based on content and available space**, not on the device. A role includes size, weight, and line-height; do not combine those values manually.

## Fonts

| Content        | Font                 | Decision                                                                            |
| -------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Persian        | **IRANYekanX**       | Primary Persian typeface                                                            |
| English        | **Roboto Condensed** | Same size, weight, and line-height as Persian. Its denser character is intentional. |
| Technical text | System monospace     | Only for code and technical literals                                                |

**Available fonts:** IRANYekanX supports weights 400–800 (600 = DemiBold); Roboto Condensed is variable (100–900). Use real font weights, not browser-synthesized bold.

## Typography tokens

All line-heights are unitless multipliers, identical for Persian and English. For Figma, multiply by 100 (`1.8` = `180%`). Token names use the `rds.type` prefix.

| Token             | Size          | Weight | Profile | Persian line-height | English line-height | Use for                                                                     | Avoid for                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------- | -----: | ------- | ------------------: | ------------------: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `caption-sm`      | 12px          |    400 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Optional timestamps, update notes, minor chart metadata                     | Required information, errors, actions                          |
| `caption-md`      | 14px          |    400 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Secondary metadata, card bylines, dates and status details                  | Main content or interactive labels                             |
| `ui-sm`           | 14px          |    400 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Compact list details, table cells, filter values, short secondary UI text   | Paragraphs or primary mobile actions                           |
| `ui-md`           | 16px          |    400 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Primary menu text, navigation items, list content and selection values      | Headings or long-form reading                                  |
| `label-sm`        | 14px          |    500 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Compact buttons, chips, column labels, small/medium control labels          | Long explanations or prominent mobile CTAs                     |
| `label-md`        | 16px          |    500 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Form labels, primary buttons, tabs and prominent touch controls             | Paragraphs and decorative headings                             |
| `body-sm`         | 14px          |    400 | Reading |                1.95 |                1.95 | Multi-line help text, validation explanations, supporting descriptions      | Short table values or buttons                                  |
| `body-md`         | 16px          |    400 | Reading |                1.95 |                1.95 | Default paragraphs, guides, reports and dialog explanations                 | Dense list rows or control labels                              |
| `body-lg`         | 18px          |    400 | Reading |                1.95 |                1.95 | Short introductions, onboarding leads and prominent explanatory text        | Long mobile paragraphs or compact cards                        |
| `title-sm`        | 16px          |    600 | Heading |                 1.7 |                 1.7 | Task/card titles, list-item names, small groups and compact mobile headings | Main page titles                                               |
| `title-md`        | 20px          |    600 | Heading |                 1.7 |                 1.7 | Dialogs, sheets, panels, large cards and roomy KPI values                   | Repeated dense rows or narrow KPI columns                      |
| `heading-section` | 24px          |    600 | Heading |                 1.7 |                 1.7 | Main page sections and substantial report sections                          | Small cards, mobile dialogs or every subsection                |
| `heading-page`    | 24–32px fluid |    700 | Heading |                 1.7 |                 1.7 | Primary page title, normally once per page                                  | Card, sheet or nested section titles                           |
| `display`         | 32–64px fluid |    700 | Display |                 1.6 |                 1.6 | Marketing heroes, welcome screens and expressive product moments            | Routine app screens, forms or dashboards                       |
| `input-touch`     | 16px          |    400 | UI      |                 1.8 |                 1.8 | Editable input values and placeholders on touch devices                     | Input labels, hints or buttons                                 |
| `code`            | 14px          |    400 | Fixed   |                 1.6 |                 1.6 | Standalone code, commands and technical snippets (LTR)                      | Regular UI copy; inline code should inherit parent line-height |

**Profiles:** `UI` = short interface text and controls · `Reading` = multi-line prose · `Heading` = structural titles · `Display` = expressive large text · `Fixed` = code only.

## Applying the approved fonts

The base `TYPOGRAPHY` export keeps the shared role metrics. Use `TYPOGRAPHY_BY_SCRIPT` from Typography.ts when a complete style with an explicit font family is needed:

| Content | Complete-style selection | Font binding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persian | `TYPOGRAPHY_BY_SCRIPT.fa[role]` | `rds.font.family.fa` |
| English | `TYPOGRAPHY_BY_SCRIPT.latin[role]` | `rds.font.family.latin` |
| Standalone code in either context | `TYPOGRAPHY_BY_SCRIPT.fa.code` or `TYPOGRAPHY_BY_SCRIPT.latin.code` | `rds.font.family.code` |

All 16 roles are available in both selections. These styles are derived from the existing role definitions and font tokens, so font size, weight, line-height, profile and fluid-heading formulas stay the same. The existing explicit code-font override takes precedence over the surrounding language.

Choose the content-script selection explicitly; these exports do not inspect text or choose RTL/LTR direction. For mixed text, apply the appropriate font to each language run while preserving its parent role metrics. Inline code continues to inherit its parent size and line-height; the standalone code role is not an inline-code reset. Font assets must still be loaded by the consuming application. No letter-spacing adjustment is introduced by this binding.

## Direction and mixed-language text

Persian and RTL are the default. Use logical `start`/`end` for placement and keep DOM, reading and keyboard order consistent. **Font selection follows the script, not text direction.**

| Content            | Rule                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Persian            | RTL; align to `start`. No justification, manual Kashida or decorative letter spacing.                                     |
| Standalone English | LTR; use Roboto Condensed.                                                                                                |
| Mixed text         | Follow the main language's direction; isolate numbers, URLs, emails and technical identifiers where needed.               |
| User input         | Use the appropriate direction (such as `dir="auto"`); preserve what the user typed.                                       |
| Numbers and tables | Display Persian digits except in technical literals. Right-align amount columns without switching the whole table to LTR. |
| Icons and charts   | Mirror only direction-dependent icons; do not automatically flip logos, media controls or time axes.                      |

## Responsive behavior

The **same tokens** apply at all widths. Only page and display headings change size fluidly; layout, wrapping, and role selection handle smaller screens.

| Token          | CSS size                                              | Range   |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `heading-page` | `clamp(1.5rem, calc(1.357143rem + 0.714286vw), 2rem)` | 24–32px |
| `display`      | `clamp(2rem, calc(1.428571rem + 2.857143vw), 4rem)`   | 32–64px |

| Mobile situation                 | Recommended choice                                                             |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Task or list card                | `title-sm` + `ui-sm`; `caption-md` for secondary metadata                      |
| Form or bottom sheet             | `title-md` + `label-md` + `input-touch`; `body-sm` for help/error explanations |
| Primary page header              | `heading-page`; allow wrapping and shorten the title where possible            |
| Sections inside compact screens  | Prefer `title-md`; reserve `heading-section` for major sections                |
| Two-column KPI with long numbers | Use `title-sm` or move to one column; do not shrink text arbitrarily           |
| Long-form content                | `body-md` on every screen, with flexible text containers                       |
| Marketing or onboarding          | `display` only where its height will not obstruct the main action              |

## Usage rules

- **Hierarchy:** Use the defined typography roles. Make text bold only when it needs emphasis. `caption-md` is for metadata; `ui-sm` is for short interface text.
- **Legibility:** Keep essential UI text at **14px or larger**. Reserve 12px for optional metadata. Touch inputs remain 16px; touch-target size is controlled by the component, not the font size.
- **Text behavior:** Wrap important text and allow components to grow. Never reduce font size to force a label into one line or clip required content inside a fixed-height control.
- **Mixed-script typography:** Inline English inherits its parent size and line-height; code uses LTR direction.
- **Reading width:** Use `rds.type.layout.measure.reading`, a maximum of `42rem` (672px at a 16px root). Let the text column fill available space and shrink below the cap on narrow containers. Wider page layouts use the same reading cap. The previous 48rem allowance is retired. The legacy `rds.type.layout.measure.wide` name temporarily aliases `reading`; it is not a separate wider preset.
- **Reading paragraphs:** Use `1em` only between consecutive paragraphs in reading content, such as articles, reports and multi-paragraph help text. The gap follows the paragraph font size: 16px text gets a 16px gap; 18px text gets an 18px gap. This is paragraph separation, not line-height or a general interface-gap rule.
- **Interface spacing:** Fields, cards, labels and sections use the existing shared spacing scale. Keep the approved text-layout relationships: `8px` (`rds.space.100`) between a title and its description, and `16px` (`rds.space.300`) between a section heading and its content. Apply spacing through the layout/text recipe, not implicit margins in every typography role.
- **Accessibility:** Text must stay visible when the screen is narrow (320px), the text is doubled in size (200%), or users increase text spacing. Allow wrapping and growth; never clip or overlap content. Use heading levels (`h1`–`h6`) in the correct order.

### Reading paragraph spacing

Keep `rds.type.layout.gap.paragraph` / `TEXT_LAYOUT.gap.paragraph` as the existing `1em` CSS recipe. Apply the separation once between adjacent reading paragraphs, in the paragraphs' font-size context. A wrapper's `gap: 1em` follows the wrapper font size, so it represents this rule only when that matches the paragraphs. Do not add the gap automatically after every text element, use it for interface-element gaps, or replace it with a fixed 16px value.

This is an explicit text-relative recipe exception to the px spacing-scale policy. Store its proportional rule outside ordinary DTCG dimension tokens; preserve the existing export name and CSS behavior. [USWDS typography guidance](https://designsystem.digital.gov/components/typography/#whitespace) supports em-based paragraph separation. Check the result with the approved Persian and English fonts; the unit alone does not establish readability.

Allow users to override paragraph spacing to at least twice the font size without losing content or functionality. This is an adaptability check, not a requirement to set the default gap to `2em`. See [WCAG Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing).

## Responsive layout check

A browser-based fixture tested task cards, financial KPIs, a form, reading content and headings with the current values. Fonts were **substitutes**, not the production IRANYekanX/Roboto Condensed, so this verifies layout behavior only—not final glyph rendering or readability with real users.

| Test                      | Observation                                                                                     | Design implication                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 320px viewport            | Sample task card ~211px high; long section heading 3 lines; narrow KPI value wraps              | Avoid large headings within compact cards; adapt KPI columns          |
| 360–390px                 | Same task card ~158px; KPI fits one line in the tested fixture                                  | Reflow and component width matter as much as token choice             |
| 200% text-size simulation | No document-level horizontal overflow in flexible fixtures; content became substantially taller | Do not use fixed-height text containers; validate each real component |

**Experimental comparison (not adopted):** Changing UI line-height from `1.8` to `1.65` and heading from `1.7` to `1.5` reduced the sample 320px task card from ~211px to ~193px. This is a geometry result only; test the actual fonts and reading comfort before considering any value change.

**Status:** The token roles and mobile usage guidance above are recommended. This is not a production-app audit or a human readability study. Before release, check real fonts at 320/360/390px in Persian, English and mixed text, including forms, tables, dialogs and text enlargement.

## References

- [Adobe Spectrum — Typography](https://spectrum.adobe.com/foundations/typography/typography-system)
- [Atlassian — Applying typography](https://atlassian.design/foundations/typography/applying-typography)
- [Material 3 — Type scale](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)
- [WCAG — Reflow](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/reflow) and [Text Spacing](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/text-spacing)

Veil & Shadow.md.text:
# RDS — Veil & Shadow Foundations

Veil creates **translucency and background blur**. Shadow creates **visual elevation**. They are separate systems: a component may use either, both, or neither, depending on its behavior.

## Veil tokens

Each veil **group** contains two tokens: `.color` is a theme-specific fill with alpha already included; `.blur` is a backdrop-blur dimension. Higher levels are more opaque and use less blur. A group organizes the two settings; it is not itself a token.

| Group            | Role        | Light           | Dark            | Blur | Recommended use                                                 |
| ---------------- | ----------- | --------------- | --------------- | ---- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rds.veil.100`   | Atmospheric | `#FFFFFF / 4%`  | `#2B2B2B / 4%`  | 64px | Decorative glass and background effects                         |
| `rds.veil.200`   | Ambient     | `#FFFFFF / 18%` | `#252525 / 18%` | 48px | Atmospheric overlays and floating layers                        |
| `rds.veil.300`   | Lightweight | `#FFFFFF / 52%` | `#1A1918 / 56%` | 36px | Short labels and simple panels on controlled backgrounds        |
| `rds.veil.400`   | Functional  | `#FFFFFF / 72%` | `#1A191B / 76%` | 24px | Floating toolbars, flyouts, dropdowns, popovers                 |
| `rds.veil.500`   | Focused     | `#FFFFFF / 92%` | `#1A191B / 92%` | 16px | Content-rich floating panels, expanded navigation, glass modals |
| `rds.veil.scrim` | Scrim       | `#140C11 / 52%` | `#2B2529 / 52%` | 24px | Blurred backdrop **behind** floating modals                     |

### Public token paths

| Group            | Color token            | Blur token            |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------- |
| `rds.veil.100`   | `rds.veil.100.color`   | `rds.veil.100.blur`   |
| `rds.veil.200`   | `rds.veil.200.color`   | `rds.veil.200.blur`   |
| `rds.veil.300`   | `rds.veil.300.color`   | `rds.veil.300.blur`   |
| `rds.veil.400`   | `rds.veil.400.color`   | `rds.veil.400.blur`   |
| `rds.veil.500`   | `rds.veil.500.color`   | `rds.veil.500.blur`   |
| `rds.veil.scrim` | `rds.veil.scrim.color` | `rds.veil.scrim.blur` |

For example, `rds.veil.400` is the Functional group; apply `rds.veil.400.color` as `background-color` and `rds.veil.400.blur` as the `backdrop-filter` blur radius. CSS variable names are `--rds-veil-400-color` and `--rds-veil-400-blur`.

**Veil rules**

- Apply the color as `background-color` and blur as `backdrop-filter: blur(...)`. Opacity is already in the color; **do not** set CSS `opacity` on the whole component.
- Use `100–200` mainly for decoration; use `300` only on controlled backgrounds. Check contrast for readable or interactive content on `400–500`.
- Provide an opaque fallback when blur is unavailable or transparency is reduced. Validate text, icons and controls against the actual background.
- `rds.veil.scrim` is a **group** for a blurred scrim treatment. Its `rds.veil.scrim.color` token is separate from `rds.color.scrim.modal`; keep the treatments distinct.

## Shadow tokens

All shadows use black, with `x = 0` and `spread = 0`. Only offset, blur and opacity change by level and theme.

| Token           | Role                | Y / Blur    | Light opacity | Dark opacity | Recommended use                                                                                                |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ----------- | ------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rds.shadow.sm` | Subtle elevation    | 2px / 6px   | 6%            | 14%          | Raised or hover cards, sticky headers/toolbars, specified buttons                                              |
| `rds.shadow.md` | Contextual floating | 8px / 20px  | 10%           | 20%          | Menus, popovers, date pickers, autocomplete, tooltips, toasts                                                  |
| `rds.shadow.lg` | Modal elevation     | 16px / 36px | 14%           | 26%          | Large navigation flyouts, modal and confirmation dialogs, expanded contextual panels, non-modal floating drawers |

**Shadow rules**

- **No shadow by default.** Ordinary cards, table rows, inputs and layout containers primarily use surface contrast and spacing.
- Choose elevation by **behavior**, not size. A small dropdown can need `md`; a large static card can need none.
- Use `lg` for modal and confirmation dialogs. It is the maximum shadow level for modal and non-modal elements. The scale contains only `sm`, `md` and `lg`.
- Use **one shadow token per surface**; do not stack shadow levels.
- **Shadow ≠ z-index:** shadow shows elevation; z-index sets stacking order.

## Extension guidelines

- Keep **veil** (`color` + `blur`) and **shadow** (`box-shadow`) as independent foundations. Combine them only in component recipes that need both.
- Use the existing token levels before adding new ones; introduce a token only for a distinct, repeatable purpose.
- Preserve light/dark pairs and document every new token with its use cases, exclusions and accessibility considerations.
- Treat the TypeScript token definitions as the current value reference; generate CSS/Figma exports from a single canonical registry when established.

# Context selection

**Approved foundation rules.** The executable selector is [context.mjs](master-tokens/scripts/context.mjs); its settings and enhanced-contrast mappings live in [context-policy.json](master-tokens/context-policy.json).

| Setting | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Appearance | Follow the operating system by default. An explicit app choice of light or dark overrides it. Use light when no system preference is available. |
| Contrast | Handle separately from appearance. Native forced colors take priority and use system colors; otherwise an explicit standard/more choice overrides the system contrast preference. |
| Enhanced contrast | Apply the five approved overrides for the selected appearance after shared and appearance tokens. Other roles keep their theme values and require component testing. |
| Language | Select Persian (`fa`) or English (`latin`) explicitly per content run. The code role keeps its monospace override. Fonts, direction and mixed-script segmentation remain application responsibilities. |

The enhanced overrides map `canvas` and `base` to their surface roles, and `primary`, `secondary` and `tertiary` to their ink roles. This is an accessibility override of light/dark, not a third appearance.

Applications pass current preferences to the selector and rerun it when preferences change. When `useSystemColors` is true, component CSS must use native system colors; do not apply the custom enhanced palette. The selector returns this requirement and suppresses custom overrides. It does not add preference listeners or forced-color CSS to an application.

This policy does not choose density, reduced-motion behavior, number-formatting defaults or new presentation artwork. Publishing and application integration follow canonical adoption.
